sentences.text: Unlike other rauisuchians, a group of large Triassic predators, Stagonosuchus has only a slight thickening on the ilium instead of a prominent ridge.
The pubis bone in this animal is broad and plate-like, differing from the narrower pubis with a foot-like extension seen in other genera.
The vertebrae of Stagonosuchus have constricted centra, though less so than in other rauisuchians like Saurosuchus.
Neural canals in Stagonosuchus extend into the vertebrae, creating deep concavities.
Stagonosuchus vertebrae feature many laminae, which are ridges of bone.
Fossils of Stagonosuchus were found in the Middle Triassic Manda Formation in Tanzania.
Friedrich von Huene first classified Stagonosuchus as a rauisuchid when he named the genus in 1938.
The type species of the genus Stagonosuchus is Stagonosuchus nyassicus.
Stagonosuchus belongs to the parent group Suchia.
Stagonosuchus is classified as a reptile.
Stagonosuchus is classified as an extinct paracrocodylomorph that may be a loricatan synonymous with Prestosuchus or a poposauroid.
A 2010 study placed Stagonosuchus in a basal position within Rauisuchia, outside both Rauisuchidae and Prestosuchidae.
A 2011 study identified Ticinosuchus as the closest relative of Stagonosuchus, despite significant size differences.
Stagonosuchus lived during the Anisian age of the Middle Triassic period.
It is debated whether Stagonosuchus is a second species of Prestosuchus or a distinct genus outside Loricata.
